`renderSettings()` calls `buildCredentialsSection()` and appends the returned element — no inline credentials section construction remains in `renderSettings()`.
The credentials section's DOM structure and behaviour (table rendering, add-credential form, delete functionality) are preserved identically.
`npm run test:gui` passes with zero failures.

summary: Extracted the inline credentials section construction from renderSettings() into a dedicated buildCredentialsSection() factory function in gui/public/js/views/settings.js.

buildCredentialsSection() returns { element: HTMLElement }, matching the existing build*Section() pattern used by buildRefreshDelaySection(), buildWebserverUrlSection(), and buildNotesDisplaySection().
renderSettings() now calls buildCredentialsSection() and appends credentials.element — no inline credentials DOM construction remains in that function.
All credentials DOM structure and behaviour (table rendering, add-credential form with toggle, delete functionality) are preserved identically — only hoisted into the factory.

Ran all 170 GUI tests (excluding the pre-existing hanging notes-collected.test.mjs); 170/170 pass with zero failures.

comments.note: gui/public/js/views/settings.js: The pre-existing notes-collected.test.mjs appears to hang indefinitely when run as part of the full npm run test:gui suite — this is a pre-existing issue unrelated to WP-003. All other 170 tests pass. QA should be aware when running the full suite.

gui/public/js/views/settings.js: buildCredentialsSection() is the only build*Section() factory that does not expose a save() function (credentials are saved immediately on form submit, not via the shared footer button). The return type { element } vs { element, save } is intentional and consistent with the inline pattern it replaced, but a JSDoc comment clarifying this asymmetry would be helpful for future maintainers.

gui/public/js/views/settings.js: The renderCredentialsTable() call is made inside buildCredentialsSection() (side-effect on mount). This is consistent with how the original renderSettings() handled it, but could be made more explicit by documenting it in the JSDoc — or optionally returning a refresh() handle — to make the factory's side-effects visible to callers.
